basics.name: Jerry Yuxuan Wu
basics.summary: Statistics PhD student at the University of Toronto with a strong foundation in Economics and Computer Science. Passionate about uncovering value in large, complex datasets through robust code, efficient data processing, and actionable visualizations.

work.name: University of Toronto
work.summary: Provided programming assistance in R for data cleaning, visualization, and modelling; collaborated on journal articles concerning environmental pollution and unconventional oil and gas development.

work.name: University of Toronto
work.summary: Conducted tutorials, supported undergraduate students, and evaluated assignments across statistics and data science courses.
highlights: Courses: An Introduction to Statistical Reasoning and Data Science; Probability, Statistics and Data Analysis; Statistical Methods for Machine Learning; Statistics Aid Centre.
Facilitated weekly in-person tutorials for groups of approximately 25 students.

work.name: TMX Group
work.summary: Developed a flexible Python and regex fund fact sheet parser for PDF, TXT, and XML files stored on AWS S3; wrote SQL for data requests and quality assurance.
highlights: Collaborated on data quality assurance using DBeaver, GitHub, and Excel.
Used PostgreSQL and MySQL through Zeppelin, Redash, and DBeaver.

portfolio.name: Understanding spatial characteristics of parking violations in Downtown Toronto
portfolio.description: Analyzed approximately 1.1 million parking tickets from 2023 and 2024. Fitted Inhomogeneous Poisson Process and Log-Gaussian Cox Process models with Kernel Density Estimation covariates, and used HDBSCAN to identify violation hotspots.

portfolio.name: Predicting traffic accident severity and the effect of cannabis legalization
portfolio.description: Used regression, random forests, nearest-neighbor clustering, and neural networks to predict traffic severity in Quebec. Cleaned and processed Quebec Data Partnership data in Python and performed hyperparameter tuning and validation.

portfolio.name: Characterizing unconventional oil and gas development in the Permian Basin
portfolio.description: Automated an R ETL process for VIIRS night flare and Enverus well data, then used clustering, nearest-neighbor, and regression techniques to characterize flaring activity.

portfolio.name: Modelling hydrogen sulfide concentrations and leaks from oil refineries in Los Angeles
portfolio.description: Cleaned, validated, and mapped large datasets and shapefiles in R; used GAM and XGBoost models, cross-validation, Box-Cox transformations, and Extreme Value Theory.
